subject: Re: Finalizing volume-protection mechanism & shortfall remedy in pricing schedule
messages:
From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@cloudwave.com>, procure@procureit.com
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 24 Jul 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Volume protection mechanism — proposed structure

Hi Maria / Procure team,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier — good conversation. As promised, I put together a starting point for the pricing exhibit language that aligns to what we discussed: a combination of a guaranteed minimum (floor) for committed units, an annual lookback true-up, and a shortfall remedy expressed as credits rather than retroactive price increases. The goal is to balance predictability for your finance team while keeping our unit economics reasonable.

Key points in the attached workbook (Redwood_Pricing_Exhibit_v1.xlsx):
- Commit floor: 250M tokens per month (annualized) with a rolling 90-day lookback.
- Shortfall remedy: For any monthly shortfall vs. the floor, Cloudwave receives a service credit equal to 15% of the shortfall spend (applied to next billing cycle).
- Cap on overage protection: Credits capped at 30% of monthly invoice to avoid runaway subsidies.
- Escrow for smoothing: Option to place a 3-month buffer escrow to handle sudden ramp/decline windows (released quarterly based on actuals).

Open items I flagged in the sheet: exactly how to compute the 90-day lookback (calendar days vs. trailing calendar quarter), whether the credit should be applied as a percent of token spend or as a dollar credit, and whether ProcureIT needs a carveout for public sector purchases.

Would you be comfortable with the credit approach (vs. clawback via increased future rates)? If yes we can produce a redline for your legal and procurement.

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_Pricing_Exhibit_v1.xlsx (Excel)]

From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@cloudwave.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: procure@procureit.com
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Volume protection mechanism — proposed structure

Sergio — thanks for the summary and the workbook. The credit approach is preferable to retrospective price increases, but our procurement team needs a stronger remedy for material shortfalls. Two asks: 1) we need a defined formula for the shortfall credit (not a flat percent) that scales to the magnitude of the shortfall so it’s auditable; 2) we need a fallback if actuals fall below 50% of committed run-rate for two consecutive quarters — either right to terminate or an accelerated unwind with pro-rated refund from escrow.

Also please confirm whether the escrow balance is refundable to us on termination (pro-rated) or if it becomes a non-refundable stability fee. We typically push for refundable balances.

Cc’ing ProcureIT to make sure the wording we provide will stand up to their standard PSR (procurement service requirements).

Best,
Maria Lopez
VP, Cloud Platforms — Cloudwave Inc
[ProcureIT contact included for legal language alignment]

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Maria — procurement asks re: shortfall formula and escrow (internal)

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Maria’s reply. Procurement wants a formulaic credit and a termination/unwind fallback for severe sustained drops. My thinking: propose a tiered shortfall credit that scales by % shortfall: 0–20% shortfall = 10% credit on shortfall spend; 20–50% = 20% credit; >50% = 35% credit + right to terminate if >50% for two quarters (but require 60-day remediation notice).

Other guardrails to protect Redwood: credit cap equal to 30% of invoiced amount in any month; escrow is refundable pro-rata on termination but can only be applied to outstanding invoices / shortfall credit (no cash payouts). That mirrors our existing approach in other deals but we should avoid language that looks like an unconditional refund.

Action items I propose:
- Ben: draft numeric formula language for the exhibit (examples + calculation appendix).
- Marissa: loop legal (Neha) and prepare a redline we can send to Cloudwave.

I attached a quick redline sketch (Proposed_Redline_Pricing_Exhibit.pdf) with these bullets turned into clauses. Please review and call out anything that creates unacceptable exposure.

Thanks,
Sergio
[Attachment: Proposed_Redline_Pricing_Exhibit.pdf (PDF)]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: Maria — procurement asks re: shortfall formula and escrow (internal)

Sergio / Ben — thanks. High level legal guidance from my side:
- The tiered credit looks reasonable but replace any language that allows an external auditor to re-open invoices beyond a 180-day lookback. Keep audit rights narrow and cadence-based (quarterly).
- Escrow: we can agree to a refundable escrow on termination but only after first satisfying any outstanding invoices and shortfall credits. Do not agree to unconditional cash refunds.
- Termination trigger: allow Cloudwave termination for a sustained >50% drop for two consecutive fiscal quarters, but require a remediation period (60 days) and a final review by our RevOps to confirm metrics. Also include a mutual exit assistance clause (data export window + pro-rata fees).

Neha — can you sign off on the attached redline and add the exact clause language for the calculation appendix (examples showing a $/token vs % spend calculation)? We want to provide a clear, auditable method that procurement can accept but avoid open-ended liability.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Director, Commercial Contracts — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: see Proposed_Redline_Pricing_Exhibit.pdf]

Cc: 
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: Maria — procurement asks re: shortfall formula and escrow (internal)

Team — reviewed and added precise language to the calculation appendix. Summary of legal positions I added to the redline:
- Shortfall credit formula: credit = min(C, S * f(%shortfall)), where S = shortfall spend in USD for the month; f(%shortfall) maps to 0.10/0.20/0.35 for the tiers. Examples included.
- Audit: customer may request invoice validation once per quarter; any disputes must be logged within 90 days of invoice issuance.
- Escrow: refundable on termination after pro-rata application to outstanding invoices and credits; escrow funds are not a general cash reserve and cannot be used for other claims.
- Termination: customer may terminate for sustained >50% drop for two consecutive fiscal quarters after a 60-day remediation notice period; Redwood reserves rights to sample usage patterns to confirm cause and to offer reduced commitments as an alternative.

One open item: discounts/concession level for the commit. Marketing and Sales need to agree on maximum discount tolerance if we accept the refundable escrow + tiered credits. Sergio — what discount are you committing to? I can run quick exposure calc if you provide the concession level (e.g., 20% off list vs 10%).

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Final_Pricing_Exhibit_Redline.pdf (PDF)]

Hi Maria — thanks for the quick feedback. Attached is the redline (Final_Pricing_Exhibit_Redline.pdf) that incorporates the tiered, formulaic shortfall credit, the refundable-escrow approach with pro-rata application, and the termination/remediation language we discussed. Summary of changes:
- Tiered shortfall credit formula with examples (0–20% / 20–50% / >50%).
- Credit cap: 30% of monthly invoice.
- Escrow: refundable on termination after application to unpaid invoices and credits; no unconditional cash payouts.
- Audit: limited to one invoice validation per quarter; disputes must be raised within 90 days.
- Termination: allowed after two consecutive fiscal quarters >50% shortfall, with 60-day remediation.
